svg.aria-label: The bot's loan-to-value lines, the order it tries steps each tick, and its rules for growing, the Hyperliquid short, unwinding, paying leavers and the arbitrage.

g.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, sans-serif
g.text: Loan-to-value lines
Neverland liquidation threshold.
Panic: the bot cuts the loan below 66.5%.
The monitor pauses the vault.
Collateral never leaves past this line.
With no short profit, it sells to 56%.
The controlled unwind starts here.
It repays from the short's profit first.
The unwind stops here.
The monitor unpauses here.
Hedge margin can borrow up to here.
Target LTV.
The first build stops here.
Below this, the bot borrows back to 43%.
Carry gate
The bot borrows more only if the book earns money.
It counts staking yield, funding and borrow cost.
It also takes off 1.06% a year for running costs.
Once it passes, the check stays open for good.
The keeper's shMON arbitrage
It never runs while leavers wait.
It always leaves the WMON vault a reserve.
The reserve is half its cash or the last payout.
Its profit goes to the desk as WMON.
Each tick, the bot takes the first step with work.
0. The mode comes first.
In FullHalt, the bot does nothing.
In Paused, the bot only cuts risk.
In DegradedData, it skips growth, new shorts and payouts.
Data is stale after 60 s for blocks and 90 min for prices.
A Hyperliquid outage also counts as stale data.
In Withdrawing, the bot serves the batch.
An open intent is finished before anything else.
1. The exit desk and the stable desk take their step.
2. Over 66.5%, the bot repays, sells and halves the short.
3. Over 55%, the bot repays, takes profit and sells to 54%.
4. The bot sweeps bridge refunds, harvests and conversions.
5. A short more than 1% too small is topped up.
6. Deposits settle, stable debt moves, and leavers get paid.
7. The short is trimmed and its margin synced.
8. The bot takes profit, sells for margin, and rebalances.
9. The bot balances lenders, moves debt, sweeps and grows.
A refused desk step waits 5 minutes.
A failed loan bundle blocks bundles for 15 minutes.
Pause and prices
When paused, the bot still repays, sells, hedges and settles.
When paused, it cannot supply, borrow or pay leavers.
The monitor pauses at 66.5% and unpauses at 50% after 30 min.
A manual pause stays until someone lifts it.
The share price is in shMON and moves at most 3% an hour.
The oracle posts every 30 min, or on a 1% move.
Delta Neutral posts on a 0.2% move instead.
An empty vault ticks every 5 min and posts every 2 h.
The rules
Opening and growing
The first build takes the loan to 42% in one go.
Under 33%, the bot borrows back to 43%.
Idle shMON over $1 also starts a borrow.
It borrows only what lenders hold before the kink.
It uses USDT0 when cheaper, in $10,000 chunks.
It skips a loop under $10 or over 0.35% in costs.
It skips a loop that pays back in over 10 days.
Deposits wait for the next share price.
Growth runs only in Normal mode, with shares out.
The short on Hyperliquid
The short is shMON held less delta times equity.
On Delta One it is 0.49 times equity at target.
On Delta Neutral it is 1.15 times equity at target.
Each vault's delta is fixed on chain.
The bot resizes when off by 1% of equity and $10.
Margin is 28.57% plus fees, with a 5% buffer.
Margin tops up when it falls under 80% of need.
Margin comes from cash, a loan to 45%, or a sale.
After a cut, half the short reopens at +4%.
The rest reopens at +8% or after 48 hours.
Unwinding
The controlled unwind repays and takes profit first.
It then supplies idle shMON and sells down to 54%.
Each step trims the short by up to a quarter.
Panic cuts until the loan is under 66.5%.
Euler liquidates at 80%, so it carries more loan.
Paying leavers
The oldest batch is paid first.
Idle shMON pays it when it covers the batch.
Otherwise the bot cuts the loan and the short first.
Then it sells on Curve, uses the desk, or sells shMON.
All chain steps go out in one bundle.
Curve takes any sale over $10 under 0.15% cost.
A desk chunk is capped at 4 hours of sales.
It is also capped at 92% of the lender's room.
Any leftover under $1,000 is sold at market.
Holders who stay keep the 0.30% exit fee.
